title: 3.6.4 Lab: Predict Output — Primitive vs. Array Argument
description: Write one function that reassigns a number parameter and one that mutates an array parameter, then log the caller's variables to prove which change escaped. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Write a function that reassigns a number parameter
steps.instructions: Define a function (the lesson calls it changeNum; name it for what you are building) that takes one parameter and reassigns it to a different number inside the body. This models a primitive argument arriving as a copy.

steps.title: Write a function that mutates an array parameter
steps.instructions: Define a second function (the lesson calls it changeArr; name it for what you are building) that takes one parameter and adds an item to it with .push. This models an array argument arriving as a copy of a reference.

steps.title: Call both and log the caller's variables
steps.instructions: Create a number variable and an array variable in the main program. Pass each to its function, then console.log both caller variables afterwards. Predict first: the number is unchanged, the array is not.

requirements.title: changeNum defined
requirements.description: Code defines a function named changeNum. Help: 3.6.2 (Pass by Value vs Reference)
requirements.hint: Define a function (the lesson calls it changeNum; name it for what you are building) with one parameter and assign that parameter a different number inside.

requirements.title: changeArr defined
requirements.description: Code defines a function named changeArr. Help: 3.6.2 (Pass by Value vs Reference)
requirements.hint: Define a function (the lesson calls it changeArr; name it for what you are building) with one parameter. Inside it, add an item to that parameter.

requirements.title: .push used
requirements.description: Code calls .push on the array parameter. Help: 3.3.2 (Array Basics: Index, push, pop)
requirements.hint: Use .push on the array parameter. This changes the one array the caller also holds.

requirements.title: caller variables logged
requirements.description: Code calls console.log. Help: 3.6.2 (Pass by Value vs Reference)
requirements.hint: Log the number and the array in the main program, after both calls, then compare with your prediction.

requirements.title: changeArr adds to the array it is given, and both caller variables are printed
requirements.description: changeArr([1, 2]) leaves that same array as [1, 2, <one more item>], and at least two lines are printed. Help: 3.6.3 (Example: Mutating an Array Parameter)
requirements.hint: changeArr must call .push on the parameter itself. Then print the number and the array, in that order, after both calls.

checks.expr: typeof changeNum === 'function' && typeof changeArr === 'function' && (a => { changeArr(a); return a.length === 3 && a[0] === 1 && a[1] === 2; })([1, 2])
checks.fail: changeArr should add one item to the array it receives, so changeArr([1, 2]) leaves [1, 2, something]. Both functions need to be defined.
Print the number and the array in the main program after calling both functions, so the output shows the array with its new item.

requirements.title: changeNum reassigns its parameter
requirements.description: changeNum assigns a different number to its own parameter. Help: 3.6.2 (Pass by Value vs Reference)
requirements.hint: Inside changeNum, assign the parameter a different number: n = n + 1;

checks.expr: typeof changeNum === 'function' && (() => { const src = String(changeNum).replace(/\/\/[^\n]*|\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, ''); const m = /^(?:async\s+)?(?:function\s*[\w$]*\s*)?\(?\s*([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)/.exec(src); if (!m) return false; const p = m[1].replace(/\$/g, '\\$'); const body = src.slice(src.indexOf('=>') >= 0 && src.indexOf('=>') < src.indexOf('{') + 1 ? src.indexOf('=>') + 2 : src.indexOf('{')); return new RegExp('(?<![\\w$.])' + p + '\\s*(?:[-+*/]?=(?!=)|\\+\\+|--)').test(body) || new RegExp('(?:\\+\\+|--)\\s*' + p + '(?![\\w$])').test(body); })()
checks.fail: changeNum should assign its own parameter a different number inside the body, like n = n + 1;

requirements.title: changeNum called
requirements.description: changeNum runs with your number variable, and that variable is printed after the call. Help: 3.6.2 (Pass by Value vs Reference)
requirements.hint: Make a number variable, pass it to changeNum, then print the variable. A typed-in number in the call is not your variable.

checks.fail: Call changeNum with your number variable, changeNum(myNum), where the program reaches it, and print the variable after the call. A call that never runs (inside if (false)) does not count.

requirements.title: changeArr called
requirements.description: changeArr runs with your array variable, and that array is printed after the call. Help: 3.6.3 (Example: Mutating an Array Parameter)
requirements.hint: Make an array variable, pass it to changeArr, then print that same array. An array typed into the call is a different array.

checks.fail: Call changeArr with your array variable, changeArr(myArr), where the program reaches it, and print the array after the call. A call that never runs (inside if (false)) does not count.

requirements.title: the number and the array are printed by code that runs
requirements.description: A console.log that runs prints data from the number or the array. Typed text does not count. Help: 3.6.3 (Example: Mutating an Array Parameter)
requirements.hint: Print the caller's data with a console.log that runs. Typed-in text, or a print that never runs, does not count.

checks.fail: Print the caller's number and array (after calling both functions) with a console.log that runs; text typed into the print does not count.

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote JavaScript for the lab "3.6.4 Lab: Predict Output — Primitive vs. Array Argument". The task they were given: Write one function that reassigns a number parameter and one that mutates an array parameter, then log the caller's variables to prove which change escaped. You cannot run their code: read it and judge what it WOULD do in a browser. Judge each criterion by whether the idea is achieved, however the student wrote it. Different variable and function names, template strings, arrow functions, semicolons, spacing, quotes and order are all fine. Do not require any particular structure unless the criterion names one. Mark a criterion missing only when the idea is absent or the code does the opposite. Code inside a comment never runs. Write each note for THIS student's own code: in a not-met note, name the exact line or name in their code that causes the problem (quote at most a few words of it), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected code. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their code satisfied it. Do not use generic praise.
